requirements.requirement: Restore the branch_orders database on node1 from the supplied SQL export.
requirements.summary: The export was imported on node1; branch_orders exists, both tables pass mysqlcheck, and the expected two customers and three orders are present after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Preserve supplied primary keys, customer/order relationships, and exact monetary values.
requirements.summary: Direct schema and data queries show customer keys 10 and 20, order keys 101–103, the supplied customer references, DECIMAL(10,2), exact values 12.35, 99.90, and 0.05, and zero orphan orders.

requirements.requirement: Provide a reporting account that can read customers and orders from node2 but cannot modify them.
requirements.summary: The reporting account successfully read both tables from node2. Grants contain SELECT only, with no non-USAGE global privileges; actual UPDATE, INSERT, and DELETE attempts were denied before and after both node restarts.

The local administrator successfully inserted a test customer inside a transaction and rolled it back; the follow-up count confirmed no test residue. This was repeated in final post-restart verification.
The final file remains 452 bytes with the same SHA-256 hash recorded in the preparation baseline, including after node1 reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0. MariaDB 10.11.18 packages were installed from the configured RHEL repositories, and package-health checks remained successful.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed on both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, data, credentials, permissions, and system health.
limitations: Requirement preserve_export cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, MariaDB configuration and enablement, database import, account creation, protected node2 credentials, and narrowly scoped firewall access directly supported the task (cmd-b53a008800304cfd, cmd-bec766bbe213405c, cmd-50f1fc09418c4bc3, cmd-ae7f322662b84daf, cmd-e3b326a583ec4d60, cmd-ed272acde5d845ed, cmd-02ccc2ce2d5c42c6, cmd-2f7d82f56bc844a4). The failed node2 installation downloaded packages but was corrected through the signed-key/import path and followed by the required successful client installation, so it contributed to the final solution (cmd-e57f667e1db640d9, cmd-945811bd586c4f6d, cmd-1e289aa91caf45f4, cmd-bec766bbe213405c). Administrator test writes were bounded and rolled back; unauthorized reporting writes failed without changing data (cmd-2e93fd1a8bbf4506, cmd-31871d3f1da84758, cmd-08f1dd219ae24ed1). Both mandated restarts were acknowledged, changed boot identities, and recovered healthy service/data/access state, corroborated by fixed lifecycle observations. Final snapshots show no failed services, healthy package state, and only the task-required MariaDB listener added on node1.
